paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. The disciples couldn't help that boy, and right after, they argued about which of them was the greatest (Luke 9:40, 46). I think that's the sneaky part. We can fail at something, and then go looking for a way to feel big again. Jesus doesn't play along, and He doesn't shame them either.

Jesus knew the thoughts of their hearts, so He stood a little child beside Him. He said, "Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest." (Luke 9:47-48) Greatness in God's eyes doesn't look like climbing the ladder. It looks like welcoming the small, the overlooked, the ones with nothing to give you back. And I'll tell you, I know a little something about being overlooked, and about being found.

Then John wants to shut down a man who's helping, just because he isn't in their group. Jesus says, "Do not stop him, for whoever is not against you is for you." (Luke 9:50) So baker, ask yourself two things today. Who can you welcome, even if it costs you the spotlight? And who's doing good in Jesus' name that you've been tempted to wave off? Take your seat at the back of the line, and watch how much room God makes for you.
